status: local-preflight-passed; awaiting root review and later remote execution
scope: Source-only review, authorized local fixes, tiny synthetic temporary-directory checks and plan-only invocations. No remote actions, GPU/browser calls, live data scans or cache tree scans.

resolved_findings.issue: Diagnostic channelState can be stale and is not ordered-drain evidence.
resolved_findings.fix: Requires a launch-hash-bound capture completion handoff, authoritative active channel absent/closed, expected worker count and explicit zero pending/compile/mailbox-flight fields; records observation time and handoff hash.

resolved_findings.issue: tar -tf verifies readable member headers but not cache payload integrity.
resolved_findings.fix: Hashes ordinary source files, inventories directory/symlink entries, verifies unique exact tar member coverage, modes and every regular-file/hard-link payload against the manifest, and saves final archive SHA256 before completion.

resolved_findings.issue: GPU idleness alone does not establish that the released service has no CPU cache writers.
resolved_findings.fix: Requires successful release record with critical artifacts saved, currently empty live process group and bounded current GPU-idle check; retains declared missing cache names.

resolved_findings.issue: Signal/exit races or diagnostics failures can leave an incomplete release record; zombie-only groups can falsely block stopping.
resolved_findings.fix: Tolerates already-exited owned targets, records errors/final state in finally, bounds nvidia-smi, separates live members from retained zombie members and preserves original paused dispatcher.

resolved_findings.issue: A failed optional cache archive must not keep an idle paid pod open after critical evidence is saved.
resolved_findings.fix: After release/artifact prerequisites, failures are preserved as cache-preservation-failed-optional with stop_ready=true and stop_blocked_by_cache=false; prior attempts are retained. Such optional failures return normally without claiming a completed archive.

resolved_findings.issue: A 2x-payload-only quota estimate can miss tiny-file archive overhead; minimum one-second timeouts can outlive the nominal cap.
resolved_findings.fix: Reserves the larger of 2x payload or padded payload plus per-entry headers, with 64 MiB headroom; deadline expiration now raises instead of resetting the remaining allowance.

required.runtime_sha256: SHA256 of exact remote live runtime.json bytes
required.completed_epoch: Finite positive UTC epoch, not more than 60 seconds ahead of the release host clock

capture_completion_contract.meaning: Root supplies this only after capture confirms ordered cleanup and critical results are durably saved. The helper verifies the declaration/identity, not the browser raw evidence.

cases: missing/mismatched handoff flags, launch identity and timestamp rejected
actual open channel rejected despite stale closed diagnostic
pending work, compilation, mailbox flight, missing mailbox evidence and wrong worker count rejected
regular files, empty file, symlink and hardlink archived exactly
payload corruption rejected although tar headers remain readable
optional no-cache failure retains explicit failure and stop readiness
checks.syntax: Both modules imported by the synthetic test runner and executed in plan-only mode.

remaining_limits: No remote release, cache preservation, quota measurement or stopped-pod verification has run as part of this preflight.
Workspace quota remains the explicitly declared 160 GB budget plus filesystem free-space guard; this helper does not query provider quota.
Symlinks are preserved and verified as links; external targets are not followed or included. A complete tar does not promise arbitrary-path cache portability or cache-hit rates.
A payload manifest and byte-verified tar are the source preservation evidence. Root must inspect the recorded cache status; a normal exit can intentionally represent optional cache failure.

Process ownership is tied to the specific prepared live launch PID/group, cwd, command, server hash and runtime-hash-bound handoff. A different launch requires a separately reviewed helper adjustment.
Deadline checks cover bounded subprocesses and each streaming hash chunk. This is not an independent remote watchdog or assurance against a kernel/filesystem I/O hang.
